parsed.explanation: The combined regime is driven by national entry/document screening and federal facility exclusion. A trans visitor whose appearance, marker or records raise doubt can face refusal, secondary inspection, stranding, or a fraud ineligibility finding; if detained, the dossier documents severe abuse in immigration custody. National rules bar trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities matching identity, while the division adds a public-school bathroom ban and a minor care ban but no documented statewide adult bathroom rule. Adult daily life in private venues is less restricted than the national framework implies, but remedies are partial and litigation unresolved. Minors and guardians face care and school restrictions plus hostile threat-framing. This sits high-risk, below organized-targeting states, above jurisdictions with only administrative friction.

entry_documents.exposure: National sex-at-birth document regime; visa/entry officers may refuse or demand extra evidence where documents/records conflict or sex is doubted; suspected wilful misrepresentation can support lifetime fraud ineligibility; detentions/stranding reported; trans-athlete entry ban.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding is not automatic, requires four elements and waiver possibilities; existing X passports remain valid until expiry; passport policy is under litigation.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor's home passport meets destination screening; appearance-marker mismatch or X marker may trigger secondary inspection; officer discretion and allied-government advisories shape outcomes.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopted conversion-style practices for trans inmates; custody reporting stopped.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts have enjoined some national orders; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; no documented custody safeguard for trans immigration detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border discrepancy can escalate to detention, where birth-sex and abusive custody practices are documented; consular access is not addressed.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities matching identity; division's 2023 law restricts trans public-school students to birth-sex facilities; no statewide adult bathroom rule documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State education guidance urges caution on school provision; local ordinances cover some accommodations; national orders face litigation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Adult visitor mostly in private venues faces federal-building exposure; travelling minor in public school would face state restriction; enforcement of school provision is unquantified.

care_services.exposure: Division bans puberty blockers and hormones for trans minors with no phase-out; national rules propose barring public insurance under 18; national order frames minor care as mutilation.
care_services.protection: Division bars conversion therapy on minors; care-ban litigation continues but ban is in force; adult visitor care access is not documented.
care_services.interaction: Adult routine care is not shown denied; trans minor cannot obtain banned care in division; emergency and visitor care remain unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritizes 'radically pro-transgender' groups; executive order directs investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; justice memo references 'radical gender ideology' though not as reward criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity; courts have enjoined some orders; 22 states plus capital outlaw gender-identity discrimination.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Chilling for visible advocacy and school settings; ordinary tourist is less targeted; minors, guardians and educators face more exposure.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division restricts trans students' school bathrooms and sports and bans minor gender-affirming care; national order threatens teachers over names/pronouns; proposed insurance bar.
minors_guardians.protection: Conversion-therapy ban; care-ban litigation; some local ordinances; national hate-crime coverage.
minors_guardians.interaction: Visitor minor not enrolled in public school avoids some school rules, but care ban and hostile climate affect any care need; parent/guardian prosecution is not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime statute excludes gender identity; no trans-specific violence statistics in dossier; outside 19 municipalities there is no local public-accommodations protection.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 19 municipal ordinances; state employment protection via national appellate ruling.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse is patchy and geography-dependent; police response to anti-trans violence is not quantified; national protections coexist with local gaps.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and executive-order litigation unresolved; border remedies slow and opaque; custody harms documented; no source quantifies school-facility enforcement or violence.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit, injunctions, legal-aid FAQ, national hate-crime law and some local ordinances.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Protections operate after harm and unevenly; at border or in custody a traveller may lack real-time remedy; adult facility enforcement remains unclear.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's border register excludes and humiliates without arrest; this regime similarly refuses or strands and adds federal facility exclusion plus documented severe immigration-custody abuse, but lacks a universal register. Slightly below 0.35, not down at 0.25, because no organized street sweeps or death penalty are documented.

Kestrel Isles has secondary screening and refused admission but administrative penalties and no documented custody abuse; here possible lifetime fraud findings and abusive detention make it materially less safe than 0.55.
Meridia has trained border officers, brief detention and tribunal appeals; here national document hostility, facility exclusion, custody abuse and patchy remedies place it far below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: National entry screening and facility rules set the floor: document mismatch can produce refusal, stranding or fraud exposure, and detention carries documented severe abuse. The division adds school-facility and minor-care restrictions but no documented statewide adult bathroom ban. National hate-crime coverage and some local ordinances are real but do not reach the border or custody; litigation may block parts of the regime, yet remedies are slow and uncertain. Adult private-venue daily life is not as restricted as the national framework, but a trans visitor remains exposed at the border, in federal facilities and if detained.
